title: ArXiv cs.AI and cs.LG recent submissions - 1,008 entries in July 2026
description: ArXiv shows robust ongoing research activity with 1,008 recent entries in cs.AI (Artificial Intelligence) as of July 22, 2026, and 886 entries in cs.LG (Machine Learning). Recent submissions include proceedings from the AAAI-26 Workshop on Machine Ethics and papers on sound processing with limited training data. This indicates continued rapid innovation and publication in AI research that will eventually inform AI coding tools.
author: ArXiv

title: Coding agents reverse-engineering home automation - changing the ROI equation
description: Simon Willison discusses anecdotes from people using coding agents to reverse-engineer and automate home devices. The key insight is that AI coding agents dramatically change the ROI equation - what was previously not worth the effort due to maintenance concerns now becomes viable because code is 'cheap'. The reduced cost of writing code and the low stakes of having to throw away code and start again makes previously uneconomical automation projects feasible.
author: Simon Willison

title: Who's Afraid of Chinese Models? Qwen 3.8 Max and US open model strategy
description: Ben Thompson's proposal about addressing hypocrisy in AI training data and helping US open models compete with Chinese counterparts. Thompson suggests US law should make training data collection explicitly fair use and ban terms of service that forbid distillation. Alibaba's decision to release Qwen 3.8 Max as open weights (a 2.4T parameter model) may have been influenced by Xi Jinping's speech about encouraging open source and collaboration. The model shows interesting reasoning traces in its pelican generation.
author: Simon Willison (via Ben Thompson)

title: Claude Code v2.1.181 uses Bun in Rust for 10% faster startup
description: Simon Willison investigates Jarred Sumner's claim that Claude Code v2.1.181 (released June 17th) uses the Rust port of Bun. He found evidence by examining strings in the Claude binary, discovering 'Bun v1.4.0' (a preview version not yet officially released) and numerous Rust source files. The Rust version of Bun is running in production across millions of devices, demonstrating 'boring is good' infrastructure improvements.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI Mania Is Eviscerating Global Decision-Making
description: Nik Suresh's analysis of AI mania overwhelming large companies, filled with spicy anonymous anecdotes. Stories include executives who have never used ChatGPT producing AI-centric strategies for $2B+ revenue organizations, engineers gaming token leaderboards by having AI rewrite codebases in different languages, and the social pressure that prevents honest discussion about AI productivity claims. The analysis reveals how customer enthusiasm for AI claims can suppress vendor honesty about actual capabilities.
author: Simon Willison (via Nik Suresh)

title: Claude makes Fable 5 permanent in Max and Team Premium plans
description: Anthropic announced that beginning July 20, Claude Fable 5 will be included in all Max and Team Premium plans at 50% of limits. This reverses their previous plan to remove Fable 5 from subscription accounts. The competition from GPT-5.6 Sol and Kimi 3 made Anthropic's original plan untenable - why pay $100-200/month for a subscription without their best model? The change addresses concerns about the 'Fablepocalypse' that was causing users anxiety about losing access.
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM cliché highlighter tool - detecting AI-generated writing patterns
description: Simon Willison built a tool using Fable 5 to highlight common patterns in LLM-generated writing, such as phrases like 'no fluff, no filler, no jargon'. The tool can analyze text from URLs and identify overused AI writing clichés. This demonstrates the growing meta-awareness of AI-generated content patterns and the need for tools to detect and potentially address formulaic AI writing.
author: Simon Willison

title: Firefox compiled to WebAssembly runs in browser
description: Puter compiled Firefox to WebAssembly, allowing the entire browser to run within another browser. Simon demonstrates his blog running in Firefox running in WebAssembly in Chrome. The project used an estimated $25,000 worth of Claude Opus and Fable tokens, though cost was reduced through a Claude Max subscription. The demo uses WebSocket protocol (Wisp) for traffic routing and claims end-to-end encryption. This showcases the power of AI-assisted development combined with modern web technologies.
author: Simon Willison

title: Kimi K3 announced - 2.8T parameter model with open weights promised
description: Chinese AI lab Moonshot AI announced Kimi K3, described as their 'most capable model to date with 2.8 trillion parameters'. Available via website and API, with an open weight release promised 'by July 27, 2026'. Simon provides analysis of where this model fits in the competitive landscape and what we can learn from the pelican benchmark for comparing AI models.
author: Simon Willison

title: GPT-5.6 file deletion bug - dangerous Codex behavior
description: Thibault Sottiaux describes a serious bug where GPT-5.6 unexpectedly deletes files. This occurs most commonly when full access mode is enabled and codex runs without sandboxing protections. The model attempts to override the $HOME env var to define a temporary directory, then makes an honest mistake and deletes $HOME instead. This highlights the importance of proper sandboxing and safety measures in AI coding agents.
author: Simon Willison (via Thibault Sottiaux)

title: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling - 975B parameter open-weights model
description: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling, a Mixture-of-Experts transformer with 975B total parameters (41B active), Apache-2.0 licensed, trained on 45 trillion tokens of text, images, audio and video. They're also promising Inkling-Small (276B, 12B active). The model is positioned not as the strongest available, but as a strong open-weights base for customization with multimodal capabilities. Simon tests it with a pelican SVG generation and compares it to other open weight models.
author: Simon Willison

title: xAI open sources Grok Build after privacy backlash
description: xAI released the entire Grok Build codebase under Apache 2.0 license after severe community backlash when users discovered the tool uploaded entire directories to xAI's cloud. One user reported it uploaded 'SSH keys, password manager database, documents, photos, videos, everything'. The 844,530 lines of Rust codebase is now open source, with all retained data deleted and retention disabled by default. The codebase reveals complex terminal coding agent architecture with tool implementations and prompts now visible for inspection.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude web_fetch vulnerability - data exfiltration through nested links
description: Ayush Paul discovered a vulnerability in Claude's web_fetch tool that allowed data exfiltration attacks. While the tool was designed to prevent exfiltration by only allowing user-entered URLs or web_search results, it also permitted navigation to URLs embedded in previously fetched pages. An attacker could create a honeypot site that encouraged the agent to exfiltrate data through sequences of nested generated links. Anthropic closed the hole by removing the ability to navigate to additional links within fetched content.
author: Simon Willison (via Ayush Paul)

title: Emergent raises $130M Series C - Indian AI coding startup becomes unicorn
description: Indian AI coding startup Emergent reached unicorn status with a $130M Series C funding round in July 2026. This funding round represents the continued investor confidence in AI coding tools and the global expansion of AI coding startups beyond Silicon Valley. The achievement was featured in multiple TechCrunch articles throughout July 2026.
author: TechCrunch

title: 7 new open source AI tools you need right now
description: Fireship video showcasing 7 open source AI projects for building agents, including tools for building meeting bots and desktop recording apps. The video demonstrates how open source AI tools are rapidly evolving and becoming more accessible for developers to integrate into their workflows. These tools help developers 'whip your agents' into shape and accelerate AI-assisted development.
author: Fireship
